stages.title: The Theory
body: Prepare the café
One cold item. One stock line. Your role.
Start when the adult confirms readiness.
stages.notes: Untimed. Introduce the practical, stock sheet and role card. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!C9; Lesson register!F12. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

stages.title: Arrival task
body: Three tips: greet politely; repeat the order; ask if unsure.
Which tip could help today?
What is an allergen?
You are unsure about a filling. What do you do?
What comes before food preparation?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Self-contained retrieval reminder is printed in the resources. Expected: a tip with a useful reason; something that can cause an allergic reaction; stop and ask the responsible adult to check approved information; wash and dry hands before food handling. Do not invite personal allergy disclosure or promise suitability. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

stages.title: Hygiene check
body: Look at the practice scene.
Find three things to put right.
Point, say or write a safe next step.
We discuss the errors. We do not act them out.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Use the authored three-panel illustration, replacing the source photo without changing the hygiene purpose. A: phone on preparation board; move it away, adult arranges board cleaning, wash/dry hands after touching it. B: loose hair above fruit; tie it back and rewash after touching hair. C: watch and bracelet; remove as directed, then wash/dry hands. This is an illustrated practice scene, not the actual recipe. Do not introduce a real unsafe scene.

visual.caption: Illustrated practice scene with three errors. Not an actual recipe or completed practical. Do not copy the actions.

panels.scene: A phone is on the food preparation board.
panels.fix: Move the phone away. The adult arranges cleaning of the board; wash and dry hands after touching the phone before food handling.

panels.scene: Loose hair hangs above the fruit.
panels.fix: Tie hair back before food handling. Wash and dry hands again after touching hair.

panels.scene: A watch and bracelet remain on the preparation wrists.
panels.fix: Remove the watch and jewellery as directed by the adult’s hygiene procedure, then wash and dry hands before food handling.

stages.title: Make one approved cold item
body: 1 Wash and dry hands.
2 Read the approved recipe.
3 Check ingredients with the adult.
4 Make one cold portion.
5 Present and store as agreed.
6 Clean down your station.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Model the full six-step sequence with one approved fruit pot. Proposed training fruit pot: one portion in one clean pot; 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit A plus 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit B. The adult must approve the actual fruit names, ingredient labels, amounts, suitable pot and utensils, and storage before use. These are authored training amounts, not a verified actual menu. No ingredient or item is claimed to be allergen-free. Adult performs ingredient/allergen and storage decisions; learner uses approved pre-cut ingredients, no knife. Model weighing one amount, assembling, presenting, handing over for storage and cleaning. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

visual.caption: One step at a time. Ask when you are unsure.

stages.title: Sequence and count together
body: Put the six recipe steps in order.
Count one stock line together.
Training example: 6 pots, 2 used, 4 left.
What is your first job before food handling?
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Use actual mixed sequence cards B/E/D/A/F/C as the correct letter order. The source shared stock lines are cups, lids and napkins; choose one available line and count it physically. The six-pot model is labelled training only. Hinge: starting assembly before the adult ingredient check is not ready. Wash/dry hands and resolve the check before making food.

stages.title: Prepare your cold item
body: Follow the six-step card at your own station.
Make one approved portion.
Supported: use pre-cut ingredients and assembly help.
Independent: follow the full approved sequence.
Aspire: check portion consistency with the adult.
stages.notes: 12 minutes. First part of the source 18-minute You Do. Adult completes readiness before real preparation. Learner sequences cards, prepares and presents one item, and follows the agreed storage handover. Adult records actual actions and prompts on VOC4-L1-E1. A quality check of another station is only through the adult, without touching another learner’s food or forcing pair work. route_tasks.Supported: Use pre-cut approved ingredients, one step at a time, with agreed reading or assembly support recorded. MCQ access orders the six mixed cards, then makes the item.
route_tasks.Independent: Follow the complete approved preparation sequence and explain any check you needed.
route_tasks.Aspire: Check that the portion matches the approved amount; discuss a station quality check through the adult.

stages.stage: YOU DO record or clear down
stages.title: Count stock and choose your role
body: Count your actual stock line. Record the amount.
Agree your role: serve or prepare.
Write or tell your first job.
Give two opening checks for your role.
stages.notes: 6 minutes. Completes the source 18-minute You Do. VOC4-L1-E2 contains actual stock and personal role fields. Offer front-of-house or back-of-house/quiet preparation role under adult direction. Suitable checks include approved ingredients/allergen information confirmed with the adult, clean utensils/work area, stock count and practice-money readiness. Record individual choices and support; do not copy training counts.

route_tasks.Supported: Count one line with a number track or adult prompt. Choose an agreed quieter role and two checks from the prompt card.
route_tasks.Independent: Count and record one line, complete your role card and explain two opening checks.
route_tasks.Aspire: Recount to resolve a mismatch and explain how a check protects the service.

stages.title: Store tidy and file
body: Follow the adult’s storage and clean-down plan.
Keep your recipe record, stock count and role card.
Record the help you used.
I checked __.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Safely hand over or store the actual item under the approved plan; do not assume it can remain until the next lesson. A fresh approved batch may be required for the Mission. File actual observation and evidence using the evidence app. Product photo is item-only and subject to local permission; no identifying people or labels. Record actual minutes after teaching.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: Name one hygiene check you made.
What is your agreed café role?
My check was __. My role is __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Accept a private spoken, signed, pointed or scribed response. Link the check to the learner’s observed work rather than merely copying the model. If only rehearsal occurred, say so and identify the missing readiness step.

stages.title: Key words
body: Role: your agreed job.
Hygiene: keep food and the work area clean.
Allergen: something that can cause an allergic reaction.
Stock: items ready to use or serve.
Float: practice money at the start.
Clear down: put away and clean.
Feedback: a useful comment.
stages.notes: Untimed reference. Read and show the concrete items. An allergy question always goes to the responsible adult; do not ask learners to diagnose or advise.

support_pages.title: Opening reminder and recipe
lines: Three useful service tips: greet politely; repeat the order; ask the responsible adult when unsure.

Proposed training fruit pot: one portion in one clean pot; 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit A plus 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit B. The adult must approve the actual fruit names, ingredient labels, amounts, suitable pot and utensils, and storage before use. These are authored training amounts, not a verified actual menu. No ingredient or item is claimed to be allergen-free.
Use only the recipe and ingredients confirmed on the adult readiness record.

rows: Wash and dry your hands. Wash thoroughly with liquid soap and warm running water, rinse and dry thoroughly. Ask the adult if help is needed.
Read the approved recipe. Point to the two approved pre-cut fruits, amounts and clean pot. Do not start until the adult has confirmed the recipe.
Check with the adult. The adult checks the actual ingredient labels, allergen information and storage plan. Do not guess or promise that food is safe.
Make one cold portion. Use the approved utensils. Weigh the approved amounts into one clean pot. No learner cutting is needed.
Present and store as agreed. Keep the pot rim clean, fit the approved lid if used, and ask the adult where and how to store the item.
Clean down your station. Deal with used utensils and surfaces under the adult’s instructions. Leave the area ready for the next task.

support_pages.title: Mix and sequence the recipe
lines: Read, point or cut out these six steps. Put them in a safe order before making the item.
The adult may read the cards. Your own order is recorded on the evidence sheet.
This selection task alone does not prove that you prepared food.

support_pages.title: Stock and role prompts
lines: Worked training example only: 6 clean pots at opening; 2 used; 4 remain. Your actual count may differ.
Count each item once. Move counted items aside if the adult agrees. Recount if unsure.
Serve role: welcome, repeat the order, hand over the order, wait for adult release of food, say thank you.
Prepare role: check with the adult, make approved portions, pass the correct item through the agreed handover, keep the station ready.
Possible opening checks: adult ingredient/allergen check complete; clean utensils and work area; enough stock; practice money ready.
Choose two checks that fit your agreed role. Ask for a quieter station if needed.

paragraphs: The workbook photo starter is supplied as a clear authored three-panel practice illustration: A phone on preparation board; B loose hair over fruit; C watch and bracelet on preparation wrists. paragraphs: Model one actual stock count using cups, lids or napkins if available. The separate worked example of 6 pots minus 2 used equals 4 left is training only. Assign each learner one real stock line and record the unit.

staff_answers: Arrival: useful service tips are greet politely, repeat the order and ask when unsure. An allergen can cause an allergic reaction. An uncertain filling or ingredient question means stop and ask the responsible adult to check accurate approved information. Wash and dry hands before food handling.

Hygiene check illustration: A phone is on a preparation board; B loose hair hangs above fruit; C a watch and bracelet remain on preparation wrists. Suitable fixes are move phone away and have the adult arrange board cleaning; tie hair back; remove watch/jewellery as directed. Wash and dry hands after touching a phone or hair and before food handling. Discuss the picture; do not enact an unsafe scene.

Mixed recipe cards are B, E, D, A, F, C: wash/dry; read the approved recipe; adult ingredient/allergen check; assemble; present/store; clean down. Selecting cards is access to the task, not proof that the practical occurred.

The proposed fruit pot uses two approved pre-cut fruits at authored training amounts of 50 g each in one clean pot. The adult must confirm actual ingredients, amounts, labels, storage and equipment. No ingredient or item is declared allergen-free. The real readiness record must be completed before food handling.
Worked stock example: 6 opening pots minus 2 used leaves 4. Actual counts are determined by physically counting the assigned real line; do not copy 6 or 4 into the learner’s actual stock record.

Relevant opening checks include the adult-confirmed ingredient/allergen record, clean equipment/work area, counted stock and practice-money readiness. Accept two checks appropriate to the agreed serve or prepare role. An Aspire check of another station is adult-mediated.

Record only actual learner actions, prompts, counts and storage handover. Mark a rehearsal honestly. Product photos are of the actual item only if locally permitted; no person or identifying label is required. Blank forms, adult models and planned 40 minutes do not establish completion.

Which tip could help today?
What is an allergen?
You are unsure about a filling. What do you do?
What comes before food preparation?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
slides.notes: 4 minutes. Self-contained retrieval reminder is printed in the resources. Expected: a tip with a useful reason; something that can cause an allergic reaction; stop and ask the responsible adult to check approved information; wash and dry hands before food handling. Do not invite personal allergy disclosure or promise suitability. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

slides.title: Hygiene check
body: Look at the practice scene.
Find three things to put right.
Point, say or write a safe next step.
We discuss the errors. We do not act them out.
slides.notes: 2 minutes. Use the authored three-panel illustration, replacing the source photo without changing the hygiene purpose. A: phone on preparation board; move it away, adult arranges board cleaning, wash/dry hands after touching it. B: loose hair above fruit; tie it back and rewash after touching hair. C: watch and bracelet; remove as directed, then wash/dry hands. This is an illustrated practice scene, not the actual recipe. Do not introduce a real unsafe scene.

visual.alt: Synthetic three-panel practice scene: A phone on a food preparation board; B loose hair above fruit; C watch and bracelet on preparation wrists. Not an actual learner photo.
visual.caption: Illustrated practice scene with three errors. Not an actual recipe or completed practical. Do not copy the actions.

panels.scene: A phone is on the food preparation board.
panels.fix: Move the phone away. The adult arranges cleaning of the board; wash and dry hands after touching the phone before food handling.

panels.scene: Loose hair hangs above the fruit.
panels.fix: Tie hair back before food handling. Wash and dry hands again after touching hair.

panels.scene: A watch and bracelet remain on the preparation wrists.
panels.fix: Remove the watch and jewellery as directed by the adult’s hygiene procedure, then wash and dry hands before food handling.

slides.title: Today I can
body: Prepare a cold item safely, count opening stock and complete a personal role card for the café.
I can follow the approved recipe.
I can count my stock line.
I can name my role and two opening checks.
slides.notes: Untimed. Exact source outcome. [QUAL] — agreed planner activity. These I-can lines are classroom checks, not official criterion quotations.

slides.title: Make one approved cold item
body: 1 Wash and dry hands.
2 Read the approved recipe.
3 Check ingredients with the adult.
4 Make one cold portion.
5 Present and store as agreed.
6 Clean down your station.
slides.notes: 5 minutes. Model the full six-step sequence with one approved fruit pot. Proposed training fruit pot: one portion in one clean pot; 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit A plus 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit B. The adult must approve the actual fruit names, ingredient labels, amounts, suitable pot and utensils, and storage before use. These are authored training amounts, not a verified actual menu. No ingredient or item is claimed to be allergen-free. Adult performs ingredient/allergen and storage decisions; learner uses approved pre-cut ingredients, no knife. Model weighing one amount, assembling, presenting, handing over for storage and cleaning. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

visual.caption: One step at a time. Ask when you are unsure.

slides.title: Sequence and count together
body: Put the six recipe steps in order.
Count one stock line together.
Training example: 6 pots, 2 used, 4 left.
What is your first job before food handling?
slides.notes: 5 minutes. Use actual mixed sequence cards B/E/D/A/F/C as the correct letter order. The source shared stock lines are cups, lids and napkins; choose one available line and count it physically. The six-pot model is labelled training only. Hinge: starting assembly before the adult ingredient check is not ready. Wash/dry hands and resolve the check before making food.

slides.title: Prepare your cold item
body: Follow the six-step card at your own station.
Make one approved portion.
Supported: use pre-cut ingredients and assembly help.
Independent: follow the full approved sequence.
Aspire: check portion consistency with the adult.
slides.notes: 12 minutes. First part of the source 18-minute You Do. Adult completes readiness before real preparation. Learner sequences cards, prepares and presents one item, and follows the agreed storage handover. Adult records actual actions and prompts on VOC4-L1-E1. A quality check of another station is only through the adult, without touching another learner’s food or forcing pair work. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

route_tasks.Supported: Use pre-cut approved ingredients, one step at a time, with agreed reading or assembly support recorded. MCQ access orders the six mixed cards, then makes the item.
route_tasks.Independent: Follow the complete approved preparation sequence and explain any check you needed.
route_tasks.Aspire: Check that the portion matches the approved amount; discuss a station quality check through the adult.

slides.stage: YOU DO record or clear down
slides.title: Count stock and choose your role
body: Count your actual stock line. Record the amount.
Agree your role: serve or prepare.
Write or tell your first job.
Give two opening checks for your role.
slides.notes: 6 minutes. Completes the source 18-minute You Do. VOC4-L1-E2 contains actual stock and personal role fields. Offer front-of-house or back-of-house/quiet preparation role under adult direction. Suitable checks include approved ingredients/allergen information confirmed with the adult, clean utensils/work area, stock count and practice-money readiness. Record individual choices and support; do not copy training counts.

route_tasks.Supported: Count one line with a number track or adult prompt. Choose an agreed quieter role and two checks from the prompt card.
route_tasks.Independent: Count and record one line, complete your role card and explain two opening checks.
route_tasks.Aspire: Recount to resolve a mismatch and explain how a check protects the service.

slides.title: Store tidy and file
body: Follow the adult’s storage and clean-down plan.
Keep your recipe record, stock count and role card.
Record the help you used.
I checked __.
slides.notes: 4 minutes. Safely hand over or store the actual item under the approved plan; do not assume it can remain until the next lesson. A fresh approved batch may be required for the Mission. File actual observation and evidence using the evidence app. Product photo is item-only and subject to local permission; no identifying people or labels. Record actual minutes after teaching.

slides.title: Exit ticket
body: Name one hygiene check you made.
What is your agreed café role?
My check was __. My role is __.
slides.notes: 2 minutes. Accept a private spoken, signed, pointed or scribed response. Link the check to the learner’s observed work rather than merely copying the model. If only rehearsal occurred, say so and identify the missing readiness step.

slides.title: Key words
body: Role: your agreed job.
Hygiene: keep food and the work area clean.
Allergen: something that can cause an allergic reaction.
Stock: items ready to use or serve.
Float: practice money at the start.
Clear down: put away and clean.
Feedback: a useful comment.
slides.notes: Untimed reference. Read and show the concrete items. An allergy question always goes to the responsible adult; do not ask learners to diagnose or advise.

body: Adult readiness before any real food handling.
Individual station and supervised utensils.
Record actual actions, counts and support.
A rehearsal is not the completed practical.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Prepare a cold item safely, count opening stock and complete a personal role card for the café. Source: Medium Term Plan!C9; Lesson register!F12. Autumn 2 Week 4 Theory. No teaching date is inferred.

Prepare one approved cold item, count an actual stock line and agree a role with two opening checks. This bundle contains two vocational lessons only; the separate Careers interview lesson is outside scope.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split practical 12 and stock/role 6; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slide are untimed.
The adult prepares ingredients and the work area in advance so the learner can assemble rather than cut. Do not hurry a food-safety check to fit the clock. Record actual work and any unfinished step.

planner_sections.heading: Adult readiness and approved recipe
paragraphs: Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

Proposed training fruit pot: one portion in one clean pot; 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit A plus 50 g of approved pre-cut Fruit B. The adult must approve the actual fruit names, ingredient labels, amounts, suitable pot and utensils, and storage before use. These are authored training amounts, not a verified actual menu. No ingredient or item is claimed to be allergen-free.

Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.

The adult records actual fruit names, quantities and ingredient/allergen information on the supplied readiness form. Check labels again if an ingredient changes. There is no learner knife task. The proposed example is not permission to serve a particular item to a person with an allergy.

planner_sections.heading: Starter and model
paragraphs: The workbook photo starter is supplied as a clear authored three-panel practice illustration: A phone on preparation board; B loose hair over fruit; C watch and bracelet on preparation wrists. Corrections: move phone away and adult arranges board cleaning; tie hair back; remove watch/jewellery as directed. Wash/dry hands after phone or hair contact and before food handling. Do not stage an unsafe actual scene.

Model all six steps: wash/dry hands; read approved recipe; adult ingredient/allergen check; assemble one portion; present and follow storage instructions; clean down. The mixed-card answer is B, E, D, A, F, C.

planner_sections.heading: Stock and personal role
paragraphs: Model one actual stock count using cups, lids or napkins if available. The separate worked example of 6 pots minus 2 used equals 4 left is training only. Assign each learner one real stock line and record the unit.

Learner agrees a serve or prepare role and two opening checks. Individual stations remain. A station quality check for Aspire goes through the adult; it does not create forced peer pair work or let learners handle one another’s food.

planner_sections.heading: Evidence and learner ownership
paragraphs: VOC4-L1-E1 includes adult readiness, the learner’s recipe sequence, actual practical observation and item-only product photo reference if locally permitted. VOC4-L1-E2 includes actual opening stock and a learner-owned role card.

The observer records the individual’s own action and support. If readiness fails, use empty-pot/card rehearsal if useful, keep its record clearly labelled and leave the real-preparation outcome incomplete. Do not invent a photo or actual food action.

planner_sections.heading: Regulation and recording
paragraphs: BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

Use individual stations and agreed handovers through the responsible adult. No forced peer pair work, cold calling or class performance. Adults may read, rephrase and scribe exact words. They record prompts, actual actions and individual contribution; they do not invent observations or complete the learner’s choices. A plan, model or blank form is not completed evidence.

Lundy Space: quieter individual station. Voice: choose or agree a role and communicate checks. Audience: adult listens and records. Influence: improve a count or presentation after feedback. Use agreed local feedback codes only.

Record actual date, active minutes, contribution, support and observer initials after teaching. Do not assume the prepared item can be stored until Mission; follow the actual approved storage/use plan or prepare a fresh approved batch. File genuine evidence in the evidence app.
